purpose: triage of the 66 reachable target-bounded unresolved element-7 sites; analysis and planning only, no rule change

source_identity.note: the admitted install is the V1 frozen candidate; the working tree may be a descendant, so obligations are joined to the inventory at the inventory's own source head, not the working tree

predicate_element_7.basis: AGENTS.md section 7 criterion 2: a required precondition may be established by an external ABI contract
predicate_element_7.why: 66 reachable unresolved site(s) are not contract-bounded, and/or an unclassified site is reachable

groups.label: SLH-DSA static adrs-function table stored in a key field
groups.mechanism: function pointer table stored in a struct field and reloaded; single writer selects one of two const tables
groups.why_not_fired: S2b refused writer-set-incomplete for SlhDsaKey.adrs_func even though source has one writer; the image-wide instruction scan did not prove the writer set.
groups.evidence: Enumerate the single source writer hash_ctx.rs:252 assigning ossl_slh_get_adrs_fn(...), which returns one of the two const METHODS tables in adrs.rs; enumerate every member of both tables (all must be in-image function starts) and rerun S2b with that writer set.
groups.falsifier: A second writer (e.g. key deserialization), a non-static return from ossl_slh_get_adrs_fn, or a table member that is not an in-image function start.

groups.label: provider-fetched method-struct slot (EvpKem)
groups.mechanism: vtable/dispatch slot loaded from a provider object returned by EVP_KEM_fetch
groups.why_not_fired: fetch_slot_witness has a witness for EvpKem.newctx (offset 0x28) only; these sites read offsets 0x30/0x40/0x80/0x88 whose OSSL_FUNC_KEM_* ids are absent from the slot table, so no per-call-site witness is emitted.
groups.evidence_kind: declared-ABI parameter with checkable forwarding (per-call-site fetch-slot witness)
groups.evidence: Add witness entries for each offset naming the OSSL_FUNC_KEM_* id, the writer (EVP_KEM_fetch/evp_kem_from_algorithm filling the slot from the provider dispatch entry), and the provider interface; require the base to be the fetch return.
groups.falsifier: The offset is written by any path other than the documented provider fetch, two OSSL_FUNC ids alias the same offset, or the base is not the fetch return.

groups.label: application callback parameter forwarded from an exported/internal API
groups.mechanism: genuinely dynamic application-supplied pointer passed as a parameter, then spilled, loop-carried or wrapped
groups.why_not_fired: export_callback_witness requires the operand to resolve to a single linear entry parameter; here the value is spilled to a frame slot, carried across a loop, or passed through a private wrapper/default fallback, so _param_of_operand returns non-param. The same parameter IS contract-bounded elsewhere (e.g. CRYPTO_cbc128_decrypt param 5 has 2 contract-bounded sites).
groups.evidence: Extend export_callback_witness parameter provenance to frame spill/reload and loop-carried copies whose only reaching definition is the entry parameter, keeping the existing header-typedef, .dynsym and caller-chain requirements. For do_pk8pkey/pkcs12_gen_mac also enumerate the in-image fallback (PEM_def_callback / default keygen) so the finite in-image values are explicit.
groups.falsifier: Any reaching definition of the called register that is not the entry parameter or the documented in-image fallback; an in-image caller passing a different callback; a header that does not declare the parameter as a function pointer.

groups.label: provider cipher context hardware/method table
groups.mechanism: vtable/dispatch slot loaded from a function-pointer table stored in a provider cipher context (ctx.hw / base.hw)
groups.why_not_fired: The call base is a pointer field of a provider context; S1 requires the base object to be proven as the function declared context parameter and refused ctx-not-proven-parameter, while S2b refused writer-set-incomplete/no-pointee-layout. The 72 S1-resolved sites are the same shape with a proven base and complete constructor cohort.
groups.evidence: Per context type, source-enumerate every store to the hw (or equivalent) field in its constructors and prove each stored value is a declared static function table (AES_GCM_HW, DES_*_HW, ...) whose members are in-image function starts; prove the call base derives from the function declared ctx parameter or a cast of it. Reuse S1/S2b; no new instrument.
groups.falsifier: A store of a runtime/CPUID-selected or application/ENGINE-supplied table, an open/opaque store, an unprovable context type or pointee layout, or a member that is not an in-image function start.

groups.label: legacy EVP cipher-data function field
groups.mechanism: function pointer stored in the EVP_CIPHER_CTX cipher-data struct and reloaded
groups.why_not_fired: The base is the cipher_data(ctx)/data(ctx) return, not the declared ctx parameter, and the stored block/stream_ecb function is installed by the AES/SM4 init-key path, which S2b cannot associate with the call base.
groups.evidence: Enumerate every store to EvpAesKey.block and Sm4Key.stream_ecb in the init-key functions, prove each value is a declared in-image function, and prove the cipher_data type/offset from the declared context.
groups.falsifier: An ENGINE or application can install a custom EVP_CIPHER with a different cipher-data layout/function pointer, or the base type/offset is unprovable.

groups.label: decoder method object slots from ossl_decoder_from_algorithm
groups.mechanism: vtable/dispatch slot loaded from a provider decoder-method object
groups.rule_match: ABI_CONTRACT_PROVIDER / fetch-slot shape (new slots); nested_static_instance fallback
groups.why_not_fired: The base is the return of the internal ossl_decoder_from_algorithm constructor, not an EVP_*_fetch return, so fetch_slot_witness does not recognise it; slots +0x30/+0x38/+0x50 have no witness.
groups.evidence_kind: declared-ABI parameter with checkable forwarding (constructor + provider slot witness)
groups.evidence: Witness the writes of ossl_decoder_from_algorithm to +0x30/+0x38/+0x50 and their OSSL_FUNC_DECODER_* ids, and prove the base is that constructor return.
groups.falsifier: The decoder method object can be built from an application/legacy method with arbitrary fields, or a slot is written outside the constructor.

groups.label: application/internal callback registered into a list and reloaded
groups.mechanism: value produced by a registration API and later called after being stored in a heap/global node
groups.rule_match: store-writer witness plus ABI_CONTRACT_EXPORT_CALLBACK (OPENSSL_atexit) / reachable-caller-target (rcu); no exact approved rule
groups.why_not_fired: The callback is not a live parameter at the call: it is stored in a node by OPENSSL_atexit (exported) or ossl_rcu_call (internal) and reloaded at cleanup/drain, so the witness sees a node base, not the parameter.
groups.evidence_kind: declared-ABI parameter with checkable forwarding plus a per-slot store witness
groups.evidence: Prove node.handler is written only by OPENSSL_atexit callback parameter and node.func/data only by ossl_rcu_call cb/data, then apply the exported contract for OPENSSL_atexit and enumerate the finite internal callers of ossl_rcu_call.
groups.falsifier: Another writer of the node slot, a node constructed by an external caller, or aliasing/overlap with another list.

groups.label: PBE registry row keygen slot
groups.mechanism: registration-table dispatch: function pointer copied from a runtime PBE_ALGS stack or the static builtin_pbe row
groups.rule_match: registry dispatch (reg-top); no approved rule family
groups.why_not_fired: EVP_PBE_find_ex returns keygen/keygen_ex copied from either PBE_ALGS or builtin_pbe; the call is through a stack-spilled copy (reg-top) and no rule covers a function pointer selected by a registry lookup.
groups.evidence_kind: new analysis: registry store witness plus declared-ABI registration contract
groups.evidence: Complete source enumeration of builtin_pbe (34 rows) and a per-slot witness that PBE_ALGS rows are written only by EVP_PBE_alg_add_type/EVP_PBE_alg_add, whose keygen/keygen_ex parameters are documented callbacks; combine the two arms.
groups.falsifier: A row written outside the exported registration APIs, a provider-fetched function stored in a row, or cfg-conditional builtin rows not enumerated.

groups.label: OSSL_STORE loader object method table
groups.mechanism: vtable/dispatch slot loaded from a registered or fetched OSSL_STORE_LOADER object
groups.rule_match: ABI_CONTRACT_PROVIDER for fetched loaders; no rule for application-registered loaders
groups.why_not_fired: OSSL_STORE_open_ex calls loader->field; the loader is selected from the STORE loader registry (legacy registered loaders and fetched provider loaders), so neither a static table nor a single exported parameter is provable.
groups.evidence_kind: new analysis: object-slot witness plus declared-ABI registration contract
groups.evidence: Two-arm witness: (i) OSSL_STORE_register_loader application-supplied OSSL_STORE_LOADER (declared ABI) and (ii) provider OSSL_STORE_LOADER_fetch slots; per-field witness for p_open/p_load/p_eof/p_close/... naming writer and interface.
groups.falsifier: A loader field written outside those two interfaces, or a provider loader with NULL/other functions that the interface does not admit.

groups.label: configuration module registry row init/finish
groups.mechanism: function pointer stored in a CONF_MODULE registry row and reloaded
groups.rule_match: registry dispatch; no approved rule family
groups.why_not_fired: module->init/finish are loaded from a CONF_MODULE row in supported_modules; rows are written by CONF_module_add (application callback parameters) and by DSO module loading, and no rule covers registry-row function pointers.
groups.evidence_kind: new analysis: registry store witness plus declared-ABI registration/DSO contract
groups.evidence: Store-writer witness for CONF_MODULE.init/finish (CONF_module_add and module_add from DSO), a declared ABI contract for CONF_module_add two callbacks and the DSO module entry points, and enumeration of built-in modules.
groups.falsifier: Another writer of the row; the DSO path not contract-covered; module name/DSO identity unproven.

groups.label: core BIO / BIO method dispatch
groups.mechanism: vtable/dispatch slot loaded from a BIO object reached through OSSL_CORE_BIO
groups.why_not_fired: The call is through a field at +0x18 of the BIO obtained from the OSSL_CORE_BIO handle; BIO methods are application-extensible (BIO_meth_new), so neither an in-image static set nor the existing provider contract applies.
groups.evidence_kind: new analysis: exact-slot re-derivation plus BIO-method provenance/contract
groups.evidence: Re-derive the exact slot (offset 0x18 does not match bread in the current BioMethod layout) and the base object; then either enumerate static BIO_METHOD writers (if the handle is always library-constructed) or establish a declared ABI contract for the core-BIO/BIO-method interface.
groups.falsifier: The base is an application BIO with an arbitrary method, or the offset is not a documented method slot.

instruments.instrument: registry/object-slot store witness for application-registrable function pointers
instruments.reason: the call target is stored in a registry/loader/list node that an exported registration API or DSO/provider entry can fill; a source-backed static set is incomplete and a plain parameter witness cannot see the store.
the exact method slot is not yet identified and BIO methods are application-extensible (BIO_meth_new), so no static set or existing provider witness applies.

recommendation.why: Six sites close from one source-proven writer and two const tables with no rule widening; it is the cheapest complete closure and its falsifier is immediately checkable. Follow with fetched_provider_method (two slots, existing fetch-witness shape) before the 16-site exported-callback extension.

notes: No verifier or rule was changed. No element-7 progress is claimed.
Target sets are not recorded for these sites (target_set=[] in the sidecar); admitted_target_count is the over-approximated admission set size, not a proven bound.
The core_bio_object_table site needs an exact-slot re-derivation before any closure attempt.
